text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
- Lower Saxony premier Gerhard Schroeder advises his fellow Social Democrats (SPD) to compromise with government over tax reform plans.
- New designs and location to be considered for a Holocaust memorial in Berlin.
- Giving back east German businesses to their rightful owners could last until 2015, official says.
- Row erupts over future average level of pensions.
- Hopes sink of compromise between government and SPD over income tax.
- Saxony premier Kurt Biedenkopf calls for suggestions for a 32-hour week not to be rejected out of hand.
- Exhibitors at this year's Hanover trade fair more optimistic about future prospects than they were a year ago.
- Spiegel magazine says pool of German banks lead by Commerzbank will give Kirch group credit line of 1.5 billion marks.
- Finance policy experts from both government and opposition expect huge "hole" of up to 20 billion marks in federal budget by the end of the year.
- SPD says qualification for European monetary union (EMU) scarcely possible because of state of federal finances.
- Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel calls on Tehran to stick to its commitment to the safety of German citizens.
- IG Chemie trade union distances itself from proposal for 32-hour working week made by IG Metall leader Klaus Zwickel.
